revision_summary: Five quotes in script_coverage carry correct wording but wrong timestamps (all flagged as minor, wrong_ts, not fabrications of content): (1) 'I think I just clicked on a link...' is actually at ~05:59-06:04, not 05:53 (05:53 is the rep's question); (2) 'It's 1874 Amies Ridge Court' is at ~01:59-02:04, not 00:43 (00:43 is the rep stating the wrong address); (3) 'I would say it's probably about $300 or so' is at ~06:58-07:00, not 06:38 (06:38 is the rep asking about the electric company); (4) the credit score quote is at ~07:24-07:29, not 07:08 (07:08 is the rep stating the qualifier); (5) 'At the moment, no. I'm actually not home right now' is at ~08:18-08:23, not 07:48 (07:48 is the rep asking for the bill). Fix: correct all five ts values in script_coverage to match where the customer actually speaks the quoted words -- the 'ts' field appears to be capturing the start of the exchange/rep-prompt rather than the customer's actual response timestamp; align to actual speaker utterance time. Additionally: (a) reclassify the 09:41 'company line' cherry-pick moment away from 'protocol_violation' to something like 'inconsistent_explanation' or fold it as a sub-point of the 08:26 personal-phone moment rather than a separate schema citation, since bill_collection.stewart_automated_bill_capture.detection_today only covers the personal-number anti-pattern, not self-contradiction under conversational pressure; (b) add a time_burn_detection entry or note in the trajectory verdict quantifying that a large share of the ~10-minute call (roughly 03:10-09:11) was consumed by personal/career/rapport tangents (real estate career chat, Mormon joke, son-matchmaking joke) rather than qualification or booking content -- this is a schema-named analysis directive that was under-surfaced despite being highly relevant to why the call ended without an appointment; (c) soften the qualification-signal framing on the pool-ownership cherry-pick moment (02:51) to note it as the analyst's inference rather than an established Ion qualification factor, since no schema section supports pool ownership as a usage signal.
